name: Sealand

flag.description: A red triangle at the upper hoist and a black triangle at the lower fly, divided by a broad white diagonal band rising from the lower hoist to the upper fly.
flag.symbolism: Red is said to stand for the founder, Roy Bates, black for his pirate-radio past, and the white band for a path of virtue.

hook: Sealand splits red from black with a white band climbing to the top right; Trinidad and Tobago runs a white-edged black band down across all-red.
trivia: Sealand occupies HM Fort Roughs, a Second World War sea fort in the North Sea about 11 km off the coast of Suffolk.
Roy Bates, a pirate radio broadcaster, proclaimed the platform a principality in 1967; no state recognises it.
